# PR #2952: Patch: daily super run failed

Closes #2941

## What changed and why

Two independent root causes, one per failed job of run 41660039742. No test skipped, disabled, or weakened; no lint suppressions; no spec changes.

**`web (audio, fx, asset and daily tests)` — stale `transformed` expectation in `apps/web/src/fx/flavorExits.test.ts`.** #2908 deliberately rerouted the transform family (`transformed`, `fused`, `upgraded`, `degraded`) through one shared `transmute` motif, proven by `systemMoments.test.ts`'s R2784000 describes and `cues.test.ts`'s B16 pins (which #2908 updated). `flavorExits.test.ts` still pinned the pre-#2908 two-burst smoke, and since PR CI skips `src/fx/`, #2908 merged without updating it — the daily run caught the drift. The updated case pins the exact transmute output (Nerd/arcane look, `FX_MOTIF_PHASES` timings) in the file's existing named-constant style, mirroring `cues.test.ts`'s B16 pin, keeping exact-equality strength.

**`e2e component (chrome)` — match-bar clock wraps at 390px (`apps/web/src/game/board.css`).** B46's match route at 390x664 scrolled 9px (`expected 673 to be at most 664`). Measured cause: the `.match-bar`'s clock span wrapped word-by-word into 4 lines (bar 75px tall, not one); the phone rule cut only the first span with an ellipsis. The tall chrome row left the board ~544px, `--card-h` hit its 44px floor, and board content spilled 15px past the board, 9px past the screen. #2916's tray channels (+36px fixed parts, +18px budget) ate the slack that had hidden this. Fix: `.match-bar > .clock { flex: none; white-space: nowrap; }` in the phone game-screen rule — exactly what S11 and `clock.css` document ("the match bar is one line", "the urgent pill keeps its words"). The hero tray and allowance logic were innocent; no changes there. New B46 pin asserts the clock renders one line box (Range rect count) at 390x664.

## How tested

- `JACKIOH_DAILY=1 pnpm exec vitest run --project web src/audio/ src/fx/ src/cards/art/convention.test.ts src/net/promote-production.test.ts src/tutorial/scripts/` — before: 1 failed (`flavorExits` transformed), 1725 passed; after: 81 files, 1726 passed, 5 skipped, exit 0.
- `pnpm --dir e2e exec cypress run --component --browser chrome` (after `sh scripts/build-wasm.sh`) — before: 664 passed, 1 failed (B46 match 390x664); after: 34 specs, 666 passed, exit 0.
- Revert checks: with the CSS fix temporarily removed, B46 match-390x664 fails (673) and the new pin fails (4 line boxes); with it, `mobile-ux.cy.tsx` is 87/87. The flavorExits failure was observed pre-edit in the full daily run.
- `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck`, `tsc -p cypress/component/tsconfig.json`, `pnpm exec eslint` on both touched test/spec files, `cargo fmt --check` — all clean. (`spec check` not needed: no ruling added; the R2784000 cite resolves to an existing note.)

## Decisions

- Updated the stale test instead of changing source for the fx failure (plan step 4 said source-first): restoring old smoke cues would contradict the ruling-backed transmute and break `systemMoments.test.ts` + `cues.test.ts`. Rejected: re-adding per-event smoke in `cues.ts`.
- Fixed the chrome row instead of the board budget or tray for the layout failure (plan step 2 said tray/allowance): probe measurements showed the tray fit fine and the 75px wrapped bar was the excess. Rejected: raising the `--card-h` 348px budget (would shrink phone cards and risk #2876's area pins) and touching `heroLayout.ts`.
- Environment (not delivered): Cypress 16.1.0 binary fetched directly from `cdn.cypress.io` (`download.cypress.io` 404s here), Xvfb run from the machine's cached root via a `~/bin` wrapper plus an `LD_PRELOAD` shim for its hardcoded `/usr/bin/xkbcomp`; WASM built with the full script.

Reviewer, look twice at: the `+36 vs +18` tray-channel/budget arithmetic in the note above (left as-is since the one-line bar restores slack — flag if you want the budget corrected anyway), and that B46's `mountMatch` still mounts a `.match-bar` no current route renders (kept: B46's requirement text explicitly demands chrome-covered fit).

### Its own review

Built and checked on `muse`. This is a draft while its own review run, on the same subscription, reviews it adversarially and fixes what it finds (up to 3 rounds); CI runs on it meanwhile. Once that review approves it, it is marked ready and auto-merge turns on.

| Round | Builder | Checks | Review |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | build, 77.4 min | green | - |

| Gate | Result | Time |
|---|---|---|
| rustfmt (`cargo fmt --check`) | pass | 6s |
| catalog (`cargo jackioh catalog check`) | pass | 498s |
| patches (`cargo jackioh patches check`) | pass | 1s |
| rulings (`cargo jackioh spec check`) | pass | 4s |

</details>

- `sh scripts/build-wasm.sh`, then `pnpm --dir e2e exec cypress run --component --browser chrome` (the component job's own command; narrow iteration to one spec with `--spec cypress/component/<failing>.cy.tsx`). Passes with zero failing specs.

- The new regression test(s) from step 5, run by the commands above and failing when the fix is reverted.
- `cargo jackioh spec check` only if a ruling note was added; otherwise not needed (no spec change expected).
## Done when

- [ ] Both job commands above pass locally from a clean tree on this branch.
- [ ] No test was skipped, disabled, quarantined, deleted, emptied, or given a longer timeout; no lint suppression or coverage change was added; no file outside this worktree remains changed and no extra worktree remains.
- [ ] `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p <touched crate> --all-targets -- -D warnings` (and the web typecheck/eslint for touched web files) pass; `catalog`/`patches`/`spec` checks pass if their inputs were touched.
- [ ] The pull request states which failed job each fix makes pass and the command that proves it.
- [ ] Any decision the task did not settle is recorded with the rejected alternative.

- Guessing the fix file before reproducing: the logs are unreachable from here, so steps 1 and 3 must name the failing spec/test before any edit; the suspects listed are leads, not conclusions.
- Flake misdiagnosed as fixed by a passing re-run: a timing-sensitive failure must get a deterministic wait or fixture change, with the new test failing reliably without the fix.
- Layout coupling: `--hero-w`, `--field-tile-max`, and the tray popover interact across the six viewports, so verify all viewports in the component run, not just the failing one.
- Hidden-information leak (rule 7): keep component/unit fixtures on `PlayerView` (`fullBoardView()`) and never assert on concealed state.
- Workflow-owned breakage: if `promote-production.test.ts` genuinely needs a `.github/` change, the bot must not make it; hand those exact lines to a person instead of working around them in source.
## Open questions

- None that block starting: the only unknowns (the exact failing spec/test names) are answered by running the two job commands in steps 1 and 3.
